investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both subsets. Because the pod never reached a running state, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a VM identity or lifecycle state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and failing the expected-output contract. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity or scheduling constraint in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the kata/peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible by affinity/selector, and those 2 are also the ones with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource constraint. A misconfigured or overly narrow selector would reduce the schedulable pool to exactly the nodes that are already at capacity.

Tertiary — a recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe runs: with only 2 such nodes and no preemption victims available, even a small number of concurrent remote agent workloads would saturate capacity.

Lower confidence — the three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran sequentially and each submitted a new pod; if prior probe pods were not cleaned up before the next check ran, they could have held kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and contributed to exhaustion across the run window (10:23–10:31 UTC).

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was left unscheduled for 127–147 seconds with the same scheduler message: 2 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, and the remote-agent-state probe could not collect any of the four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state). This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure scoped to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster serving remote agent VM workloads has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource allocation across the 2 nodes that carry that resource. Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 kata-capable nodes. As a result, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state and times out before the eval's latency threshold, preventing the runner from reaching the state-polling step and producing any evidence output. (Evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime)

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had no remaining capacity (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm), and the other 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both subsets. Because the pod never reached a running state, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1885) never returned a VM identity or lifecycle state, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent and failing the expected-output contract. This is an eval-infrastructure failure reflecting a real infrastructure capacity or scheduling constraint in the production-api environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots on the kata/peerpods-capable nodes are occupied by existing workloads, leaving zero capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector on the remote agent pod spec is too restrictive: only 2 of 6 nodes are eligible by affinity/selector, and those 2 are also the ones with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource constraint. A misconfigured or overly narrow selector would reduce the schedulable pool to exactly the nodes that are already at capacity.

Tertiary — a recent scale-down or node failure reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the level needed to absorb concurrent probe runs: with only 2 such nodes and no preemption victims available, even a small number of concurrent remote agent workloads would saturate capacity.

Lower confidence — the three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran sequentially and each submitted a new pod; if prior probe pods were not cleaned up before the next check ran, they could have held kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and contributed to exhaustion across the run window (10:23–10:31 UTC).

Of the remaining 4 nodes, none satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector constraints. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the 2 kata-capable nodes. As a result, every new remote-agent pod is immediately placed in an Unschedulable state and times out before the eval's latency threshold, preventing the runner from reaching the state-polling step and producing any evidence output. investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in sequence on 2026-06-27 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors reporting that 0 of 6 nodes could accept a new pod: 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent VM was never provisioned, and the eval runner received no evidence payload, causing all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) to be absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector. No preemption victims were available, so incoming eval pods remained Unschedulable for 127–153 seconds before the eval runner timed them out. This is a runtime infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect. The failure is localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment and is confirmed as an eval-layer failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
